evidence.senderRole: the pool paying the token out to a buyer
evidence.recipientRole: the counterparty of the taxed transfer
evidence.poolRole: a constant-product pool holding this token, used here to show that pool-side transfers are taxed
evidence.requestedAmountDerivation: the transfer is internal to a swap, so amount is reconstructed as transferToRecipient + transferToTaxDestination; the exact floor identity below confirms the reconstruction.
evidence.computation: One transfer of 928705879985028714768262 emits two Transfer events with the same sender: 914775291785253284046739 to 0xe355948b78b6fae494ab1fc682d03e5bc428b89d and 13930588199775430721523 to 0x82cc61354d78b846016b559e3ccd766fa7e793d5. fee = floor(amount * 1500 / 100000); transferToRecipient = amount - fee reproduces BOTH emitted amounts EXACTLY, so the measured tax is 69652940998877153607615000/464352939992514357384131 bps == 150 bps up to the one-base-unit floor residue.
evidence.corroboration: the same floor identity at 150 bps holds on 20 independent two-leg transfers of this token found by replaying eth_getLogs, 2 of which have the pool 0xf722d04773ed0642d3092d7947f29668d31b8a61 as an endpoint (2 pool->user, 0 user->pool).
evidence.reproduce: eth_getLogs on address 0x82cc61354d78b846016b559e3ccd766fa7e793d5 at block 31773591 for topic0 0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef, then group by (transactionHash, topics[1]) and look for the two legs sharing this sender.

note: Fee-on-transfer token: a taxed transfer emits TWO Transfer events with the SAME sender -- 98.5% of the amount to the intended recipient and 1.5% credited to the token contract itself, which accumulates the fee for later swap-back. Both legs are in the receipt, so the split is reproducible from eth_getLogs alone with no tracing. The fee is a floored integer division, so the realised rate equals 150 bps up to a rounding residue of at most one base unit; the exact rational for the cited transaction is in evidence.taxBpsExactRational. Confirmed on 20 independent two-leg transfers, 2 of them with the pool 0xf722d04773ed0642d3092d7947f29668d31b8a61 as an endpoint, so pool-side transfers ARE taxed -- which is what makes the token unsafe as a routing hop rather than merely unusual. Smaller populations of two-leg transfers at other rates were also seen while replaying logs (300 bps x11); they are reported here for completeness rather than folded into feeBps, which carries the dominant rate that the cited pool transfers exhibit. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE -- the destination pool receives only 98.5% of amountSent, so pool.swap(amount0Out, ...) reverts K() because the demanded output assumed the full amountSent; (2) as TERMINAL OUTPUT -- no next pool and no K() revert, but the user receives 98.5% of the quoted amountOut, silently violating the minAmountOut slippage promise (delivered < quoted). Both modes are unsafe.
